text:
ACME Support (customer): Hey Redwood — our localized QA noticed a regression after yesterday's rollout. Portuguese and Arabic inputs are often getting English responses or very low-quality translations. We're shipping a localized flow next week, so this is high priority. We also saw a few 502s during the same window. Repro steps + samples below.

Ana (CS): Sorry about this — we'll dig in. Can you paste the exact request payload and a sample response you got? Which model id are you calling?

ACME Support (customer): Sure — here's a minimal repro we've been using: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Accept-Language: pt-BR' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-translate-v2","input":"Traduzir para pt: \"Como posso pagar minha fatura?\"","max_tokens":60}'
```

Expected: Portuguese output. Actual response: English (exact):

{"id":"res_abc","model":"redwood-translate-v2","output":"How can I pay my bill?"}

Also Arabic example: input: "ترجم إلى العربية: كيف أدفع فاتورتي؟" returned the same English sentence.

Ana (CS): Thanks. Does this happen every call or intermittently? Any headers or metadata you pass beyond Accept-Language?

ACME Support (customer): Intermittent. Before the rollout it was consistent. We do set Accept-Language in all calls; no other locale meta. Rollout roughly started 2026-03-15 22:05 UTC in our logs. Sometimes it returns Portuguese but very literal/awkward.

Sophie (ML Eng): That's interesting — two hypotheses: 1) requests are being routed to an English-favoring variant (language-detection or routing change), or 2) a smaller fallback quantized variant with weaker non-en capability was used. Can you share a full request + response trace for one failing call (headers + model field)?

ACME Support (customer): Attaching a snippet from our logs (redacted):

```
request_id: req_913
timestamp: 2026-03-15T22:11:37Z
model: redwood-translate-v2
headers: {Accept-Language: pt-BR, X-Client: acme-web}
response: {status:200, body: "How can I pay my bill?"}
```

Liam (SRE): We're seeing a spike in 502/503 and p95 latency around 22:08-22:17 UTC in the translate model pool. There was routing churn during the canary. Pulling traces for those request_ids now.

DeployBot: Deployment event: hash=depl_0f4c3a, started_by=@sophie-ml, started=2026-03-15T22:05:12Z, rollout->100% at 2026-03-15T22:12:03Z. Mapping change: redwood-translate-v2 now maps to variant rust-quantized-3b (auto-fallback enabled).

Matt (Oncall): If routing to rust-quantized-3b is happening automatically, that could explain degraded non-English quality. Recommend pausing rollout or reverting mapping until we confirm. Can we flip traffic back to previous variant?

Sophie (ML Eng): We shipped a language-detection tweak in the same deploy that biases low-confidence inputs toward en when the detector confidence < 0.55. Combined with the quantized 3b fallback we see both wrong-lang outputs and lower-quality non-en text. I can push a fix to respect explicit Accept-Language headers and reduce the en-prior when Accept-Language is set.

Ana (CS): Workaround for customers: add a small metadata flag to force locale, e.g. "metadata": {"preferred_language":"pt-BR"} or pass "force_locale":"pt-BR". Sophie — can the routing layer honor that immediately?

Sophie (ML Eng): Yes — quick change to prefer force_locale header should be safe. However, if fallback mapping already sent you to the smaller variant we'll need to restore the previous mapping or increase capacity for the non-quantized pool.

ACME Support (customer): We'll try the force_locale flag, happy to test. We can also share a small test set of ~40 pt/ar prompts.

Liam (SRE): Trace sample shows a route decision: capacity shortage on large model shard triggered a fallback. Request_id req_913 routed to rust-quantized-3b because of transient capacity limit, and routing also applied the new language-prior override. That combination explains EN output. We can increase capacity or revert mapping. Scaling action underway.

Matt (Oncall): Initiating rollback of the mapping to the previous model variant and pausing further rollout.

DeployBot: Rollback event: initiated_by=@matt-oncall, started=2026-03-15T22:25:40Z, mapping restored to stable-pt-variant, rollout paused.

Sophie (ML Eng): After rollback I'll run a dedicated eval on the pt/ar prompt set (run full regression suite). Also removing the language-prior default until we have stronger evidence. If you can share the customer small test set, we'll prioritize it for today.

ACME Support (customer): Shared test set via secure upload. After adding force_locale we saw immediate improvement on our side for the tests we tried—thanks.

Liam (SRE): Confirming p95 latency improved and 502s dropped after rollback and scaling. We'll keep monitoring.

Ana (CS): Thanks everyone. ACME — we'll follow up once the regression evals finish and confirm longer-term fixes. If this recurs please tag #incidents and ping oncall.

ACME Support (customer): Appreciate the quick response and the workaround. We'll keep monitoring and report any further anomalies.
